summary:
Adversarial verification of the controller-orchestration review at commit 31d512f (main). Re-read src/controller/lifecycle.rs (all), app_controller.rs 1-470, session_controller.rs 1-330, output_controller.rs 1-570, refresh_controller.rs 1-600, workspace.rs 1-580, workspace/audio_presets.rs 1-80 and 180-195, thumbnails.rs 1-130, event.rs (all), event_sender.rs 1-160, command.rs, dependencies.rs 40-70, observations.rs 1-60, state.rs 900-940, domain/audio.rs 1-45, architecture_tests.rs rule list, ui/pages/mixer.rs 1120-1155, ui/workspace.rs 160-185, ui/navigation.rs 87-93, Cargo.toml. Verifier is self-review only: no independent sub-reviewer was spawned and nothing was executed. Result: 25 findings, 7 confirmed, 18 adjusted, 0 refuted. 7 proposed splits, 2 confirmed, 5 adjusted.

Main corrections:
1. Mutex poisoning (ctrl-01, ctrl-02) is real as an inconsistency, but practically unreachable. Every critical section is a short field assignment. The only panics that can occur inside a guard are u64 overflow expects. Severity lowered: ctrl-01 high to medium, ctrl-02 high to low.
2. event.rs line numbers in ctrl-06, ctrl-14, ctrl-15 and ctrl-24 are off by about 50 lines. The file is 388 lines: AppEvent is at 229-388, SessionEvent at 235-239, Observation at 313-316, WorkspaceLoaded at 267-275, outcome_unknown at 39-45, the test module at 90-216. ctrl-06 also cited observations.rs:373-433, but that file has 204 lines; reconcile() is at 63-123.
3. ctrl-04: RefreshQueue already handles an inactive scope (app_controller.rs:276-283); only a narrow TOCTOU race remains there. Mixer and Workspace are the real cases. A fourth case was found: preset() at audio_presets.rs:35 never publishes PresetRejected when spawn_reserved refuses.
4. ctrl-06: the proposal to derive collection scoping from the event family is wrong. The current policy (event_sender.rs:9-23) cuts across the proposed families. For example, OutputCommandFailed is collection-independent while CommandFailed and PresetProgress are collection-scoped, yet all three would be 'Outcome'. The policy must stay per-variant, though it can become a method on AppEvent.
5. ctrl-10: NaN handling is the same in both paths (both give -100). The real divergence is +inf: the inline code gives 0 dB, the domain helpers give -100 dB.
6. ctrl-22: unix_ms has about 30 production call sites, not 13. It includes storage/bookmarks.rs:89, so storage depends on controller, a layering inversion.
7. ctrl-17: JoinSet does not fit, because spawn and spawn_reserved must return a JoinHandle that callers keep (app_controller.rs:279, workspace.rs:204, 258). Use the counter plus Notify option.
8. ctrl-08: SmallVec is not a dependency (Cargo.toml). Use Vec or a fixed array.
9. The proposed splits create a bidirectional dependency between the session/ and output/ modules: output needs the session scope and journal, while session/teardown needs output/shutdown. That is legal in Rust but undermines the boundary. Keep the teardown orchestration that calls OutputShutdown in the AppController layer, or pass it in as a trait object.

None of the proposals breaks architecture_tests.rs. Its rules forbid obws outside obs/, GTK in controller/storage/obs, GTK/obws in domain, storage in domain/services, and AppController in pages. domain/stats.rs, domain/output.rs and infra/clock.rs are all allowed homes.

findings.title: Mutex poison cascade: 19 lock().expect() plus 2 overflow expect() in SessionScope reach the GTK thread
findings.evidence: Every SessionScope lock (owner, slot, tasks, evidence, terminal_reason, terminals.pending) uses .expect. A poisoned lock therefore makes every later caller panic. owns_generation (214) locks owner, and AppController::accepts_scope (app_controller.rs:372-376) calls it on the GTK thread through ui/navigation.rs:176. retire() and install() lock owner and then slot, and they run on Drop paths (session_controller.rs:39-50, 246-254).
findings.recommendation: 1) Add src/controller/runtime/sync.rs with lock_recover(m) = m.lock().unwrap_or_else(PoisonError::into_inner), logging tracing::error! once. 2) Replace the 19 lock expects in lifecycle.rs, plus app_controller.rs:221,240,253,267,296,311 and workspace.rs:124,238,261. 3) Keep the 2 overflow expects (151, 278) or convert them to saturating/explicit errors; they are not lock sites. 4) Optionally make `owner` an AtomicU64, but only if every write to owner happens while the slot guard is held: next() increments owner and clears the slot under one guard, and install() checks owner and writes the slot under the same guard. Guard: the existing lifecycle tests, plus a test that poisons `evidence` (lock it in a thread that panics) and asserts accepts_scope/is_active still return.
findings.risk: Theoretical abort of the app. In practice poison needs a panic inside a guard, and the only panics possible there are u64 overflow expects (151, 278, and output_controller.rs:426).
findings.verifier_note: Counted 21 expect() calls in production lifecycle.rs. 19 are lock().expect(). Lines 151 ('session generation exhausted') and 278 ('operation IDs exhausted') are checked_add overflows, not locks. The 'caller-supplied closure' argument is weak: OperationLease::update is a private fn, and its only closures (109, 112, 115-119, 122-125) are plain field assignments that cannot panic. No critical section runs foreign code; runtime.spawn inside the tasks guard (422) does not panic on shutdown. So poison is practically unreachable, and severity drops to medium. The value is consistency and defence in depth. The double-panic-on-Drop claim is correct but only applies once a lock is poisoned. The recommendation stays sound, with the extra constraint on the AtomicU64 owner.

findings.title: Poisoned locks silently become 'command ignored' or 'disconnected' (opposite policy to ctrl-01)
findings.evidence: mark_pending (419) does pending.lock().ok()?. set_output (63-71) reads None as 'previous operation is pending', logs a warning and returns. clear_pending (191-196, 432-439), clear_bitrate_sample (session_controller.rs:240) and bitrate_kbps_since_last_sample (refresh_controller.rs:170) silently skip when poisoned. connected_client (app_controller.rs:396) and OutputController::client (173-189) map a poisoned slot to None.
findings.recommendation: Use the single lock_recover helper from ctrl-01 in controller/. Remove `.lock().ok()` and `if let Ok(mut x) = m.lock()` in output_controller.rs, session_controller.rs, refresh_controller.rs, app_controller.rs, workspace.rs:134,198,253, workspace/audio_presets.rs:14 and thumbnails.rs:49. Land this together with ctrl-11 (ClientSlot::current), which removes 7 of these sites anyway.
findings.risk: Low. The only panic that can poison `pending` is the u64 overflow expect at output_controller.rs:426. The slot is never locked across code that can panic.
findings.verifier_note: The code is as cited. I found no reachable poison source: every guarded block is a field read or write, apart from the overflow expect at 426. 'Buttons go permanently dead' needs a poisoned lock and is not realistic. Kept as a low-severity consistency fix. Drop the separate poisoned-pending test as a prerequisite; one test of lock_recover itself is enough.

findings.title: Manual RefreshData drops output readback failures that the session scan publishes
findings.evidence: app_controller.rs:260 runs `refresh_output_statuses(client, &tx).await;` and discards the returned OutputReadbackErrors (output_controller.rs:469-501, no #[must_use]). refresh_worker publishes the same value (refresh_controller.rs:345-348). After a manual Refresh, a failed GetStreamStatus/GetRecordStatus never emits AppEvent::OutputReadbackFailed. The three-step scan sequence is duplicated across both call sites.
findings.recommendation: 1) Add #[must_use] to OutputReadbackErrors; clippy -D warnings then flags line 260. 2) Extract `full_snapshot_scan(client, tx, audio_filter, valid)` into src/controller/refresh/snapshots.rs, covering lists, outputs+publish and refresh_live_data_if, and call it from both sites. 3) Test: an app_controller test where the stream readback fails, then RefreshData, asserting OutputReadbackFailed{kind: Stream}. Land the fix as its own fix: commit before any move.
findings.risk: A stale live or recording indicator after a manual refresh.
findings.verifier_note: Verified line 260 against refresh_controller.rs:345-348. No comment explains the asymmetry. Not executed at runtime. The proposed test needs a seam: app_controller's refresh_data uses connected_client() (ObsClient), not the OutputCommandClient override. The test may therefore need the obs_fixture loopback that returns an error for GetStreamStatus, or should wait for ctrl-09's port trait.

findings.title: Hand-rolled single-flight queues: a refused spawn_reserved leaves running=true and strands the request (PLAUSIBLE)
findings.evidence: refresh_mixer_scene_audio sets running=true (301), then ignores the Option returned by spawn_reserved (306-308). spawn_reserved returns None when !is_active() (lifecycle.rs:418-420). The scope goes inactive without any GTK command when the runner ends: connect task, session_controller.rs:128. The queues are rebuilt only in sync_session_scope (app_controller.rs:360-370, Connect/Disconnect) and WorkspaceController::set_scope (workspace.rs:116). workspace.rs:248-258 has the same shape.
findings.recommendation: Create src/controller/runtime/single_flight.rs: SingleFlight<J>{inner: Arc<Mutex<Slot<J>>>} with offer(job)->Admission{Started|Coalesced}, next()->Option<J> (clears running when empty), and abandon()->Option<J>. When spawn_reserved(..) returns None, call abandon() and publish the matching failure: MixerAudioInputsFailed (controller-not-connected); WorkspaceLoaded with Err; and for presets, PresetRejected{epoch, run}. Keep RefreshQueue's explicit inactive branch, but make it race-free: try spawn_reserved first, and fall back to runtime.spawn(worker) when it returns None, instead of checking is_active() first. Tests: SingleFlight unit tests, plus an app_controller test that ends the runner (FakeSessionRunner returns), then sends RefreshMixerSceneAudio and asserts MixerAudioInputsFailed.
findings.risk: The Mixer stays in a loading state until reconnect. That state is set by set_mixer_audio_loading at ui/pages/mixer.rs:1150 before dispatch.
findings.verifier_note: RefreshQueue is not affected the way the finding claims. refresh_data branches on scope.is_active() (276) and uses runtime.spawn for an inactive scope. Only a TOCTOU window remains, between the check at 276 and the spawn at 279, while the Tokio runner retires the scope. Mixer: confirmed code path. ui/pages/mixer.rs:1132-1152 dispatches without checking the connection, but whether mixer_scene_refresh_target() returns a scene after a failed or ended session is unverified, so this stays PLAUSIBLE. Workspace: ui/workspace.rs:176 guards with nav.is_current(), which requires ObsStatus::Connected (ui/navigation.rs:87-93). The workspace case is therefore less likely, since there is a window before GTK applies the Disconnected or Error event. Additional case found: preset() (audio_presets.rs:35) assigns spawn_reserved's None to preset_task without publishing PresetRejected. Severity lowered to medium because of the reachability uncertainty.

findings.title: SessionScope is a god struct: 13 fields (12 Arc), 6 responsibilities
findings.recommendation:
Split into src/controller/session/:
- identity.rs
- task_set.rs (active, failed, cancelled, tasks, spawn/spawn_reserved/cancelled/quiesce, mark_failed/failed)
- clocks.rs
- client_slot.rs
- journal.rs
- retirement.rs
Keep SessionScope as a thin delegating composite. Move one facet per commit, behind the 3 lifecycle tests, the session_controller and event_sender tests, and final_regression_tests.rs. Document the lock order in scope.rs.
findings.risk: Growth, and an undocumented lock order.
findings.verifier_note: The structural finding is confirmed. Corrections: there are 13 fields but generation is a u64, so 12 are Arc. The reviewer's facet list omitted `failed` (18, 173-179); it belongs in task_set or retirement. The observed lock order also needs fixing. Nested guards that do exist: owner then slot (150-152, 226-230, 242-244); tasks then owner (416-418, through is_active, then owns_generation); evidence then owner (267-268); evidence then terminals.pending (303 then 326-330). terminal_reason is NOT held across evidence: at 298-302 it is a temporary, cloned and dropped. Write down this corrected order.

findings.title: AppEvent god enum (about 50 variants) with recursive envelope variants; the variant policy table lives elsewhere
findings.evidence: AppEvent (229-388) mixes lifecycle, command outcomes, observations, workspace, stats and thumbnails. SessionEvent{generation, collection, event: Box<AppEvent>} (235-239) and Observation{revision, event: Box<AppEvent>} (313-316) are boxed envelopes. The collection-independence policy is in event_sender.rs:9-23. Reference counts: ui/window.rs has 83 AppEvent:: references, controller/state.rs 44, controller/observations.rs 18.
findings.recommendation: Split into src/controller/event/{mod, envelope, lifecycle, outcome, observed, workspace, stats}.rs, with a Publication{generation, collection, revision, payload} envelope replacing SessionEvent and Observation. Keep collection scoping a PER-VARIANT method (`impl AppEvent { fn collection_scoped(&self) -> bool }`) moved out of event_sender.rs. Do NOT derive it from the family. Migrate in this order: (1) AppEvent::observed() constructor (ctrl-20); (2) move the policy fn to an AppEvent method; (3) add Publication alongside, coordinating the ui/event_pump.rs + ui/window.rs channel change with the ui reviewer; (4) move families one at a time with pub(crate) use aliases; (5) delete the boxed variants. Guard: event_sender lifecycle_envelope_and_collection_admission_follow_the_same_policy (event_sender.rs:152+), the observations tests, final_regression_tests.rs and ui/window_render_tests.rs.
findings.risk: High churn. The nesting invariant is held only by convention.
findings.verifier_note: Line numbers were wrong: event.rs has 388 lines. The real positions are AppEvent 229-388, SessionEvent 235-239 and Observation 313-316. observations.rs:373-433 does not exist (the file has 204 lines); reconcile() is at 63-123. My count is about 50 variants, not 55. The reference counts 83, 44 and 18 were verified with grep. Design defect in the recommendation: the current collection-independent set (OutputCommandPending/Succeeded/Failed, OutputReadbackFailed, GraphRefreshRejected, WorkspaceAcknowledged, Connecting/Connected/Disconnected/Error) cuts across the proposed families. OutputCommandFailed and GraphRefreshRejected would sit in Outcome next to CommandFailed, PresetProgress and PresetRejected, which ARE collection-scoped. Matching on the family would silently change fencing, which is a safety regression. Keep the policy per variant.

findings.title: WorkspaceController::request: 183-line Long Method with the fence predicate copied 8 times
findings.evidence: Verified the steps: dequeue (260-267), evidence (280-289), validate (294), supersession (295-303), SetText verify (308-319), cancel check (320-327), dispatch guard with the ActivateScene activation-revision clause (332-349), ack publication (357-369), the observation read (370), evidence settle (376-386), and final publication with a now_or_never probe (387-404). The fence copies are at 154-155, 161-163, 178, 213, 295-297, 320-321, 333-339 and 387-388.
findings.recommendation: Create src/controller/workspace/job.rs with JobFence{cancellation, ticket, revision, expected_revision, tx}, is_current() and admits_dispatch(action, scope, activation_revision). Add run_job, verify_expected_text, settle_evidence and enum JobOutcome. Reuse JobFence in audio() and media(). First add a characterization test: ActivateScene rejected after a StudioModeChanged activation bump.
findings.risk: A missed clause lets a superseded mutation reach OBS.
findings.smell: Long Method, Duplicate Code, Deep Nesting
findings.verifier_note: Line ranges and fence copies verified. Note that the copies are deliberately not identical. audio() checks cancellation and scope but not revision. The supersession check at 295-297 omits accepts_current_scope. The dispatch guard adds the activation clause. The final publish check (387-388) omits accepts_current_scope, because EventSender re-checks it. JobFence needs separate methods per check level, not one is_current(); otherwise the extraction changes behaviour.

findings.title: run_event_loop: 178-line method mixing ingress, translation, side effects and resync
findings.evidence: Verified: the select is at 431-444, resync at 445-468, the match at 470-570, side effects on the scope, dirty and audio_scene interleaved, and the direct try_send for levels at 531-537.
findings.recommendation: Extract `fn translate(event: ObsEvent, next_revision: &mut impl FnMut() -> u64) -> Ingress` into src/controller/session/event_translation.rs. Ingress is {publications: Vec<AppEvent> (at most 2 items; SmallVec is NOT a dependency), effects: IngressEffects}. Add per-ObsEvent characterization tests first. Then move resync into resynchronize().
findings.risk: Fencing regressions go uncaught.
findings.verifier_note: Confirmed structure. smallvec is not in Cargo.toml, so use Vec. Ordering caveat for the pure translate: several arms call client.next_observation() and scope.observe_graph_revision() BEFORE dirty.invalidate() and invalidate_graph() (SceneRenamed 538-546, InputsChanged 547-557). Revision issue order matters for graph fencing (refresh_controller.rs:222-228), so the effects applier must replay them in the same order as today. Also, InputLevelsUpdated bypasses the bounded handoff on purpose; keep that as an explicit effect, not a publication.

findings.title: A test seam leaks into production: OutputCommandClient with a #[cfg(test)] Fake variant is matched in 9 methods plus 2 inline sites
findings.evidence: The 9 methods are endpoint, set_streaming_if, set_recording_if, retire, with_deadline, and in the OutputStatusReader impl next_observation, retire_after_timeout, read_stream_status and read_record_status. The 2 inline matches are the uncertain heuristic (140-146) and session_controller.rs:147-155,169-192. client_override sits at 37-38 and 174-182.
findings.recommendation: Define a consumer-owned OutputPort trait in src/controller/output/port.rs, implemented for ObsClient. That is allowed: the controller already imports crate::obs::client::ObsClient, and obws stays inside obs/. Delete OutputCommandClient, OutputStatusReader and client_override. Inject a port factory through ControllerDependencies. Move the 'uncertain' decision into the port (`fn outcome_unknown_after(&self, err: &AppError) -> bool`), so fakes model it explicitly.
findings.risk: Test and production behaviour diverge.
findings.verifier_note: Verified every match site. OutputStatusReader is also implemented for bare ObsClient (337-351) and used by refresh_worker through refresh_output_statuses, so OutputPort must cover that use too. Otherwise two traits survive.

findings.title: Flat AppCommand spans 6 contexts; handle() carries inline dB math and repeated cancellation sequences
findings.evidence: Verified the flat enum. The dB conversion is at 195-205. The cancellation sequences are at 132-146, 167-177 and 378-388.
findings.recommendation: 1) Group as AppCommand{Session, Obs, Workspace, Audio, Output, Media} in src/controller/command/. ui/ has 20 files that reference AppCommand. 2) Replace the inline dB code with domain::audio::sanitize_volume_db(volume_mul_to_db(volume_mul)). 3) Extract cancel_collection_scoped_work() and cancel_session_scoped_work(). Volume mapping test table: 0.0 gives -100, 1.0 gives 0, 2.0 gives 0, NaN gives -100, +inf gives -100 (this one changes behaviour; today it gives 0).
findings.risk: Divergent dB math.
findings.verifier_note: The claim of 'different NaN handling' is wrong. Inline: `NaN > 0.0` is false, which gives -100. Domain: not finite gives NEG_INFINITY, then sanitize gives -100. Same result. The real divergence is +inf: inline gives 20*log10(inf) = inf, clamped to 0 dB (full gain), while domain gives -100 (silence). Treat the switch as a deliberate behaviour change in its own commit. The 3 cancellation sequences are not identical: Connect retires the client, SetCurrentSceneCollection cancels the preset, shutdown aborts refresh_task. The helpers must keep these differences. ui importer count is 20 files, not 19.

findings.title: Primitive Obsession: raw Arc<Mutex<Option<ObsClient>>> held by 5 owners, with the read code copied 7 times
findings.evidence: Verified all 7 read copies. Writes happen only in lifecycle.rs (152, 230, 244).
findings.recommendation: Add src/controller/session/client_slot.rs: ClientSlot with current() (public to the crate) and install_if/clear (restricted to session). Use lock_recover. Mechanical; compile-guarded.
findings.risk: A future stray write breaks fencing.
findings.verifier_note: Confirmed. Visibility note: with ClientSlot in controller/session/, pub(super) lets controller::session write. If SessionScope stays in lifecycle.rs during migration, use pub(in crate::controller) until lifecycle moves into session/.

findings.title: Sub-controllers build a private SessionScope::initial and depend on a later set_scope (temporal coupling)
findings.evidence: OutputController::new (50) and WorkspaceController::new (95) call SessionScope::initial(slot). Tests construct without set_scope: session_controller.rs:451,515,691,734,780; output_controller.rs:637,704,747,795; workspace.rs:666,885; workspace_lifecycle_tests.rs:199,257. final_regression_tests.rs does call set_scope (281, 326, 608, 665).
findings.recommendation: Take the scope (and ClientSlot) as constructor parameters. Keep set_scope for rebinding. The compiler lists every call site.
findings.risk: Tests run against a detached scope.
findings.verifier_note: Confirmed, with more test call sites than cited. The output-controller tests rely on an active private scope; a detached initial scope is active. They will need SessionScope::initial passed explicitly, which keeps their behaviour.

findings.title: Stringly-typed errors (Result<_, String>, Result<(), ()>) erase the AppError kind and force probe-based classification
findings.evidence: Verified: Result<T, String> throughout. 'Uncertain' is derived from wait_retired().now_or_never() (workspace.rs:398-400, output_controller.rs:142) or retirement_reason() (workspace.rs:380, audio_presets.rs:59). EventSender returns Result<(), ()>. refresh_controller.rs:425 re-derives 'stale vs closed' using accepts_current_scope(). Mixing: validate_scope uses user_message() (418), while read_observation uses to_string() throughout (453, 461, 464, 480, 488, 494, 504, 520, 538).
findings.recommendation: Add src/controller/error.rs with CommandError (thiserror 2 is in Cargo.toml:15; AppError is Clone because AppEvent derives Clone). Localize only at the AppEvent boundary. Add SendRejected{Stale, Closed}. Migrate module by module. Change workspace.rs:805 from string contains to matching the variant.
findings.risk: Misclassified uncertain outcomes; brittle tests.
findings.verifier_note: Confirmed in substance. Minor fix: the user_message/to_string mix is between validate_scope and read_observation, not inside read_observation. audio_presets.rs:206 was not verified (I read 1-80 and 180-195). AppEvent payloads carry String to GTK (e.g. WorkspaceLoaded result, ThumbnailLoaded result), so the boundary conversion touches state.rs and ui consumers. Coordinate with ctrl-06.

findings.title: User-visible English strings bypass Fluent (CLAUDE.md i18n rule)
findings.evidence: finish_evidence writes literal English into OperationEvidence.failure, which state.rs:911-914 copies into last_stream_command_error/last_record_command_error and state.rs:920-924 into the audit. event.rs:41 appends '; OBS command outcome unknown; command was not retried'. workspace.rs:374 'OBS is disconnected' and 439 (deadline); output_controller.rs:320-322 (deadline); the thumbnails messages are all literal.
findings.recommendation: Add Fluent ids to every i18n/<locale>/scenedeck.ftl, or store a CommandError and localize at render time. Guard: every_translation_has_the_same_messages_as_english plus the ignored locale-parity test.
findings.risk: Untranslated operator-facing text.
findings.verifier_note: The outcome_unknown string is at event.rs:41, not 92 (92 is inside the test module). output_controller.rs:262-266 and 288-292 are inside #[cfg(test)] Fake arms, so they are not user-visible in production; drop them. refresh_controller.rs:332 'UI event receiver closed' only fires when the receiver is gone, so nobody sees it; drop it. The rest is confirmed.

findings.title: Boolean flag soup allows illegal states in OperationEvidence and WorkspaceLoaded
findings.evidence: OperationEvidence has 4 bools plus failure:Option<String> (55-59). unknown() (114-120) and finish_evidence (309) each re-derive uncertain. WorkspaceLoaded carries acknowledged, uncertain and action bools (event.rs:267-275).
findings.recommendation: Add an OperationPhase enum with forward-only transitions in session/journal.rs, and WorkspaceOutcome{Read, Applied, Rejected, Unknown}. state.rs:920-923 formats dispatched/acknowledged/uncertain directly for the audit, so provide accessor methods first.
findings.risk: Inconsistent audit evidence.
findings.verifier_note: The event.rs lines were wrong (WorkspaceLoaded is at 267-275, not 318-326). Phase caveat: dispatch() and acknowledge() can arrive out of the expected order. execute_control_if calls dispatch inside the predicate, and acknowledge() runs afterwards, but finish() can be called without acknowledge (audio path, workspace.rs:173-176). A strict 'refuse backwards moves' state machine must accept Admitted then Completed directly.

findings.title: ThumbnailController bypasses SessionScope and EventSender (raw try_send, runtime.spawn, Relaxed AtomicBool)
findings.evidence: Raw SyncSender try_send (57, 91, 96); runtime.spawn (73); Relaxed ordering (46, 75-95); a magic 2 s timeout (94); English strings.
findings.recommendation: Inject EventSender (scoped). Publish through tx.send or send_if, or keep try_send with a fallback on Full. Name THUMBNAIL_BUDGET. Use CommandError. Keep runtime.spawn, or use scope.spawn_reserved ONLY after confirming the drain contract (comments at 45 and 100: obws keeps unanswered request receivers, so the code drains the capture future on purpose instead of aborting it). Scope retirement aborts the future. That is acceptable only because retirement also retires the socket.
findings.risk: Thumbnails stuck on loading when the GTK queue is full.
findings.verifier_note: Code confirmed. The recommendation to spawn through scope.spawn_reserved conflicts with the deliberate drain at line 100 when the socket is NOT retired (UI cancel). Keep cancellation separate from abort. Routing through EventSender wraps ThumbnailLoaded in SessionEvent with collection fencing (it is not in the event_sender.rs:9-23 list). Check that the GTK-side ThumbnailRequest.generation check still matches, and that a collection-fenced drop does not strand the loading tile.

findings.title: quiesce() spins on yield_now, and send_if polls every 2 ms
findings.evidence: quiesce loops over tasks.lock() with yield_now (384-392) and is awaited at session_controller.rs:119, 129, 218, 235. send_if sleeps 2 ms between try_send attempts (136).
findings.recommendation: In TaskSet, keep the AbortHandle list but add an AtomicUsize live count plus a Notify. The select! wrapper in spawn_reserved decrements the count and notifies on exit, including the cancel branch. quiesce awaits notified() until the count is 0, using the enable-then-check pattern already used in cancelled() (371-381). Do NOT use JoinSet. For send_if, back off exponentially (2 ms up to 50 ms) or move to an async channel (ui reviewer).
findings.risk: Wasted CPU during disconnect or backpressure.
findings.verifier_note: Busy wait confirmed. JoinSet is unsuitable: spawn and spawn_reserved return JoinHandle<()> that callers store and await or abort (app_controller.rs:279, workspace.rs:204, 258, session tests). JoinSet::spawn returns only an AbortHandle. The counter must also cover aborted tasks: the wrapper future is dropped on abort, so decrement in a Drop guard, not after the select.

findings.title: Feature Envy: SessionController::disconnect runs the output stop protocol inline
findings.evidence: Verified: 87 lines, the output client is extracted at 143, the pending set cleared at 166, and the stop protocol runs at 168-194, including a #[cfg(test)] Fake arm.
findings.recommendation: Add OutputController::shutdown_plan() -> OutputShutdown, with confirm_stopped() and retire(), in src/controller/output/shutdown.rs. SessionController::disconnect should take the OutputShutdown value (or a `Box<dyn ShutdownPlan>`), NOT &OutputController, so session/ does not import output/. AppController builds the plan and passes it in.
findings.risk: Output stop semantics are duplicated in two places.
findings.verifier_note: Confirmed. The adjustment keeps the dependency one-way. Under the proposed splits, output/ already depends on session/ (scope, journal). If session/teardown.rs imports output/shutdown.rs, the two modules depend on each other. Passing the plan in from AppController avoids that.

findings.title: load_config_blocking returns Default config on JoinError, and FileAppConfigProvider discards the startup_notice diagnostics
findings.evidence: unwrap_or_else returns Default::default() (454-457). read_config() returns LoadedConfig{config, startup_notice: Option<ConfigStartupNotice{FirstLaunch, ReadFailed(String)}>}. FileAppConfigProvider::load_config keeps only .config (60).
findings.recommendation: Return Result<AppConfig, AppError> and map JoinError to AppError::storage, as session_controller.rs:282-284 already does. On Err, publish CommandFailed/GraphRefreshRejected and skip the scan. Change AppConfigProvider::load_config to return Result, or LoadedConfig, so ReadFailed reaches the caller. Test with a panicking provider.
